findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", violating least privilege and giving the service user account-wide control over compute, storage, serverless and monitoring. This enables data access across all S3 buckets, log/alarm tampering via cloudwatch:*, and privilege escalation via ec2:RunInstances or lambda function creation with an existing instance profile/execution role.

A permanent IAM access key is created for a highly privileged user instead of using an assumable role with short-lived credentials, and no pgp_key is supplied, so the secret and ses_smtp_password attributes are written to the Terraform state file in cleartext. Anyone with read access to state obtains account-wide credentials.

The svc_deploy_key_material output exports access key material from the key resource and is not marked sensitive, so the value is rendered in CLI output, plan artifacts and CI/CD logs. (Note: because no pgp_key is set, encrypted_secret is unset; the insecure pattern of emitting key material as a non-sensitive output remains, and the plaintext secret is still recoverable from state.)

findings.issue_category: privileged IAM user without MFA or boundary
findings.description: A long-lived IAM user is used for automation rather than an assumable role, with no MFA enforcement and no permissions_boundary constraining its wildcard inline policy. Compromise of its static key yields full account-wide access with no secondary control.

force_destroy = true allows Terraform to delete the user along with all attached access keys, policies and group memberships without manual intervention, enabling silent teardown of an identity and its audit-relevant attachments during a destroy or a hijacked pipeline run.
